name: Hazelcast
tagline: A Java in-memory data grid and stream processor that embeds in your app or runs as a cluster.
description: Hazelcast Platform combines a partitioned, replicated in-memory data grid (distributed maps, queues, locks, CP subsystem) with the former Jet stream-processing engine and a SQL layer. It can run embedded inside JVM applications or as a separate cluster accessed by Java, .NET, C++, Python, Node.js and Go clients. It is common in banking, payments and telco for low-latency shared state and event processing. Since 5.4 the Apache-licensed Community Edition only gets major/minor releases, with patch releases, security and many operational features reserved for the paid Enterprise Edition.

license.name: Apache 2.0 (Community); Hazelcast Community License for some modules

pricing.notes: Community Edition is free; Enterprise Edition adds security, WAN replication, persistence, rolling upgrades and patch releases.

scale.notes: Data is partitioned (271 partitions by default) with backups across members; WAN replication for multi-site is Enterprise-only.

strengths: Runs embedded in a JVM process or as a client-server cluster with the same API
Data grid and stream processing (former Jet) in one runtime
CP subsystem gives Raft-backed locks, semaphores and atomic references
Near-cache support delivers local-memory reads for hot data
Mature in regulated industries with long-term enterprise support
weaknesses: Community Edition gets no patch releases; security, persistence and WAN are Enterprise-only
JVM heap and GC tuning matter for large members
SQL engine is limited compared with a real database
No longer markets a vendor-managed cloud; you operate the cluster
useCases: Fraud detection and payment stream processing
Web session clustering for Java app servers
Distributed caching in front of RDBMS
notIdealFor: Non-JVM teams wanting a lightweight cache
Durable primary storage on Community Edition
